newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler CEO's pay hike angers UAW strikers.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler CEO's pay hike angers UAW strikers.

text.p: Fanning flames of anger among striking union workers, Chrysler Corp. said Friday that Chairman Robert Eaton's total compensation more than tripled in 1996 to $12.6 million.

Eaton's income, disclosed in Chrysler's annual proxy statement, included exercised stock options worth more than $4.4 million. In 1995, he earned a total of $4.1 million in salary, bonus and other compensation but did not exercise any stock options.
The disclosure came a day after United Auto Workers Local 51 struck Chrysler's Mound Road engine plant in Detroit and the automaker reported record first quarter earnings of $1.0 billion.
"It's absolutely ludicrous for him to make that kind of money when he wants to give our work away," said UAW Local 51 President Sam Nardicchio.

The strike has cut off Chrysler's only source for V-6, V-8 and V-10 truck engines, forcing the automaker to shut down four U.S. truck assembly plants and idle 12,080 workers on Friday in addition to the 1,800 strikers.
The idled plants, which build Chrysler's Jeep Grand Cherokees, Dodge Ram and Dakota pickup trucks and full-size Ram vans, are located in Detroit and Warren, Mich., St. Louis and Windsor, Ontario.

The union will not agree to a new local labour contract unless Chrysler drops plans to shift production of drive shafts from the plant to an outside supplier, Toledo, Ohio-based Dana Corp., Nardicchio said.
The move would eliminate about 250 jobs from the Mound Road plant, which already has a clouded future because its engines are expected to be phased out by the year 2000.
No formal negotiations were scheduled for the weekend, but informal, behind-the-scenes discussions are expected to take place between top company and union officials.

A source close to the talks said the lack of negotiations over the weekend was intended as a "cooling off period" for both sides. Analysts estimate that a prolonged strike could cost Chrysler about $70 million per week in lost profits.

Cashing in on near-record earnings in 1996, Eaton earned salary, bonus and other compensation totalling $8.2 million, including a near doubling of his cash bonus to $4.5 million from $2.36 million in 1995.

Chrysler said Eaton's 1996 base salary increased to $1.4 million from $1.2 million and he received $2 million under a long-term incentive plan, up from $434,981 in such payments in 1995. The total package was by far his highest since leaving General Motors Corp. to join Chrysler in 1992.
The chairman's compensation does not include a grant for new, unexercised stock options for 696,018 shares, which were given a present value of $4.5 million.

Bolstered by strong truck, Jeep and minivan sales, Chrysler's 1996 net income reached a near-record $3.53 billion, up 74 percent over the $2.03 billion it earned in 1995, a year in which Chrysler experienced a costly launch of its current minivans.

Chrysler's 66,000 UAW workers brought home profit-sharing bonuses averaging $8,000 for the company's 1996 performance, the highest among Detroit's Big Three automakers. The payout matched their record bonuses in 1994.

Chrysler Vice Chairman Robert Lutz, who has agreed to stay at the automaker for about two years following his 65th birthday in February, also cashed in big in 1996. His total compensation for the year, including exercised stock options, jumped in 1996 to $10.8 million from $4 million in 1995.
Lutz exercised options worth $5.7 million in 1996, compared with $1.1 million in 1995. He also received new, unexercised options for 267,591 Chrysler shares, valued at $1.8 million.
As a group, Chrysler's top five executives earned a total of $21.1 million in salary, bonus and other compensation in 1996, up 79 percent from the $11.8 million they earned in 1995.

Ford Motor Co. said on Monday that its chairman, Alex Trotman earned $7.1 million in 1996, including $1.3 million in exercised stock options. About $2.1 million of Trotman's pay was restricted until his retirement, but Chrysler said it placed no restrictions on Eaton's pay.
GM plans to disclose Chairman Jack Smith's 1996 compensation next week.
